 The election is just one day away. Here's what to know
 BY 
 Lydia Taylor
 Ohio 
 PUBLISHED 6:24 AM ET Nov. 02, 2026 
 PUBLISHED 6:24 AM EST Nov. 02, 2026 
 SHARE 
 OHIO — On Tuesday, residents across the Buckeye State will head to the polls to make their voices heard.
 More than 1 million Ohioans have already casted their ballots through early voting. According to the Ohio Secretary of State's Office , early voting for this year's general election have exceeded early voting numbers for past gubernatorial elections.
 The data shows 1.7 million Ohioans voted by Oct. 30. Of the votes, 1,054,916 were made in person at local board of elections offices and 624,097 were by absentee ballots, as of Monday morning.
 The numbers far exceed totals for both the 2022 and 2018 general elections. In 2022, the state recorded 1.3 million early votes, and in 2018, there were 1.46 million.
 Among the important races include the bid for the U.S. Senate seat. This year, former Democrat Sen. Sherrod Brown and GOP Sen. Jon Husted are looking to claim the spot. 
 Husted was appointed to succeed Vice President JD Vance’s vacant seat and has received the endorsement of President Donald Trump. Brown lost his race fourth term in 2024 to Republican Sen. Bernie Moreno by 3.6 percentage points.
 A recent Marist Poll shows Brown has an eight-point advantage over Husted in Ohio. 
 Another race catching national attention is the Ohio governor race. This year is Republican Gov. Mike DeWine’s last year in the position. He has been governor for seven years, starting in 2019. 
 Democrat Dr. Amy Action is going up against Republican Vivek Ramaswamy for the seat. The same Marist Poll shows Acton leads Ramaswamy by 6 percentage points. 
 The last time a Democrat won the governor’s race in Ohio was in 2006.
 There will also be quite a few local issues across Ohio for residents to decide on. Here’s what you need to know about early voting, as well as other resources to ensure your voice is heard:

 On Election Day, polls will be open from 6:30 a.m. to 7:30 p.m.
